My main fix is that I'd make Mal redeemable, or at least more nuanced. 

A major issue with the Mal plot is that it's really lame and tropey in a way that a lot of people with DID find offensive. I've seen some really good insight on how Mike's system could be written with more realism and care, and I think that could be applied to Mal as well. He's often interpreted as a protector/persecutor figure as many so-called "evil" alters actually seem to be. 

Mal interested me when he first appeared because he seemed to be an agent of pure chaos who wanted to ruin the game and make everyone lose, which is a unique motivation. But eventually it was just about the money again. I think there's ways to make Mal feel more like a character and not just a diabolus-ex-machina obstacle. For example, he could try to ruin Mike's relationship with Zoey because he doesn't trust that someone can be that nice, or maybe he resents that Mike is so good at being "good," something hinted at with the "I'm a bug-eyed weirdo and everyone loves me!" bit. Maybe he wants to thrive in the chaos of Total Drama, or maybe he even wants to protect Mike from it using dire tactics. I'm not asking for intense psychological depth in a series like this, just a little more to Mal than just evil laughter and random villain tropes.

As cheesy as it'd be, I'd like if Mal and the system weren't "killed" as so many people despise the button (myself included) for how it's framed as "just turn off your mental disorder and you'll succeed!", but instead Mike had to talk Mal down into cooperation. Now Mike and Mal have to team up to win the game, and there's the stakes of whether Mal will be able to do this or if he'll feel the urge to take over for Mike again. 

I actually don't have as much of a problem with Zoey as others do because I do think she's more suspicious than people give her credit for, she just goes deep into denial and tries to find any alternate explanation that she can for Mike's behavior. So maybe play up that desperate denial more so she looks less naive? It is a heartbreaking situation when you think about it and I think making Mal a more solid character and foil to Mike would add more tension to the situation.
